inputContract.nominalRatePercent: Nominal annual rate, not effective annual rate
inputContract.periods: Total payment periods N; independent of years

conventions: A receipt is positive and a payment negative from one consistent viewpoint. Preserve existing positive-savings UX as a separate convention.
Effective periodic rate i=(1+j/CY)^(CY/PY)-1. Continuous i=exp(j/PY)-1. j is nominal annual fraction.
A fractional N is an analytic equivalent duration; an actual payment schedule needs complete periods and a final partial payment convention.
formulaSteps: Solve PV*(1+i)^N + PMT*A_N*(1+i if beginning else 1) + FV=0.
Inverse rate: bracket within j>-CY (or all real j for continuous); report no or multiple admissible roots instead of selecting an arbitrary one.
For i != 0, let q=PMT*(1+i if beginning else 1)/i; solve N=log((q-FV)/(PV+q))/log(1+i), when positive/log-defined. Handle PV+q=0 degeneracy.
At i=0 solve PV+PMT*N+FV=0; distinguish an indeterminate duration/rate from no solution.
outputContract: optional schedule with declared final-period convention
validation: Hide/ignore the selected unknown; stale input for unknown must not constrain the solution.
Require finite values, positive frequencies, N>0 and 1+j/CY>0.
Zero periodic payment gives no identifiable duration if PV+FV=0 at zero interest.

modes.title: Accumulate an annuity
modes.formula: FV = PV(1+i)^n + PMT[(1+i)^n−1]/i.
modes.explanation: Annuity here means a stream of equal cash flows. Insurance product fees, guarantees, and mortality pricing are excluded.

inputContract.months: Integer time horizon; years*12 may be offered
inputContract.taxRatePercent: Annual tax on positive investment interest

conventions: Annual end events occur at months 12,24,...; monthly end events at 1,2,...N. Beginning events occur at months 0,12,...<N and 0,1,...N-1.
Year-two monthly contributions first occur at month13 for end timing or month12 for beginning timing. Annual increases apply independently to each stream.
Tax is settled after growth and contribution events at each year end; final partial-year settlement is an explicit optional setting. Contributions are not taxed again as interest.
Monthly effective growth derives from nominal compounding, independent of contribution event frequency.
formulaSteps: Without tax: sum each deposit multiplied by growth from its event time to the horizon; add opening-balance growth.
With tax: chronological event ledger, accumulate positive annual interest, subtract annual tax at the declared settlement boundary.
Real ending balance = nominal ending balance/(1+inflation)^years. Show contributed cash separately from investment gain.
validation: Months must be integral for this monthly-grid model; otherwise use an explicit day/date model.
Do not add an annual end contribution before a full year completes.
Require valid positive growth bases, rates within stated supported domain, and nonnegative deposits.

Common SEC deferred-load examples use min(original investment, redemption value). With front loads, this model explicitly uses each lot net of its front load as its cost basis; actual prospectus may differ.
formulaSteps: At each contribution remove front load; record net invested lot and its age.
Grow each lot under the declared annual/monthly expense convention.
Apply exit load to the selected lot basis, without inventing time-varying prospectus schedules.
Also calculate identical cashflows without fees; distinguish direct fee cash from total lost ending value, which includes foregone growth.
validation: Percent loads must lie within 0..100, expense ratio within 0..100 exclusive.

currentDefinitionEvidence.description: Estimate financing after your down payment, trade-in, rebate, taxes, and fees.

modes.title: Monthly payment
modes.formula: Financed amount = price − down − trade + trade debt − rebate + tax + financed fees.
modes.explanation: Sales-tax treatment varies by jurisdiction. Select the trade-in tax treatment and enter your applicable tax rate.

currentDefinitionEvidence.description: Calculate fixed monthly payments, interest, and an amortization schedule.

modes.title: Loan & schedule
modes.formula: Payment = P × r / [1−(1+r)^−n], where r is the monthly rate.
modes.explanation: Equal monthly payments amortize a fixed-rate loan. Extra payments reduce principal after the regular payment.

notes: Fees, variable rates, collateral requirements, and lender-specific payment conventions are not automatically included.

currentDefinitionEvidence.description: Estimate a lease payment from capitalized cost, residual value, and money factor.

modes.title: Lease payment
modes.formula: Monthly depreciation = (net cost−residual)/months; rent charge = (net cost+residual)×money factor.
modes.explanation: A typical US auto lease structure is assumed. Jurisdictions may tax leases differently.

inputContract.down: Cash down payment, or explicit percent conversion
inputContract.moneyFactor: Lease rent-charge factor; optional APR/2400 conversion

conventions: Financed principal=price-down-trade+tradeDebt-rebate+(tax+fees if financed).
Tax=salesTaxRate*max(0,price-(trade if tradeTaxCredit)-(rebate if rebateTaxCredit)). Manual policy toggles avoid pretending one state rule applies everywhere.
Trade negative equity increases principal. A negative resulting principal should not be silently accepted as a loan.
A money factor converted as APR percent/2400 is a lease pricing convention, not the loan effective APR.
formulaSteps: Compute affordable principal from the finite discounted sum of budgeted payments.
Invert the monotone piecewise financing equation for price; include the tax-base zero boundary.
If down is a percent of price, solve that coupled equation rather than subtracting a fixed amount inferred from an unknown price.
Lease: pre-tax A=(C-R)/N+(C+R)*MF, adjusted cap C=price-down-trade.
Reverse lease C=(A/(1+tax)+R/N-R*MF)/(1/N+MF). Add down/trade to recover price under this specified tax model.
validation: Reject negative term, residual, factor, or nonpositive reverse denominator.
Lease fixtures tax the monthly payment, not an upfront jurisdiction-specific levy.
Do not include taxes both in financed principal and upfront cash.

modes.title: US mortgage
modes.formula: Loan = price × (1−down payment%). Monthly payment = Pr/[1−(1+r)^−n].
modes.explanation: The schedule assumes a fixed interest rate over the entered amortization period. Ownership costs are tracked separately from loan principal and interest.

currentDefinitionEvidence.description: Calculate fixed monthly payments, interest, and an amortization schedule.

modes.title: Loan & schedule
modes.formula: Payment = P × r / [1−(1+r)^−n], where r is the monthly rate.
modes.explanation: Equal monthly payments amortize a fixed-rate loan. Extra payments reduce principal after the regular payment.

notes: Fees, variable rates, collateral requirements, and lender-specific payment conventions are not automatically included.

conventions: Monthly interest accrues first; contractual payment is applied next; extra principal applies last. Scheduled payment is unchanged; this is no-recast amortization.
Map dates by calendar month difference from firstPaymentMonth; do not count from a locale-dependent parsed midnight timestamp.
Annual extra starts in the selected month and repeats every12months, not necessarily a loan anniversary.
Duplicate one-time months are summed; last total payment is capped at accrued amount owed.
formulaSteps: Contractual PMT=principal / sum((1+APR/12)^(-k), k=1..N).
For periodk: interest=openingBalance*r; regular=min(PMT,balance+interest); apply extra=min(requestedExtra,remainingBalance).
Extra requests combine applicable monthly,annual,and one-time events. Stop when balance is zero.
Compute baseline separately at the same contractual PMT without extras; compare interest saved and payoff date.
validation: Reject malformed dates and extra dates before first scheduled payment, or explicitly ignore them with a visible reason; do not reinterpret them.
Reject negative extras; do not let an extra cause negative balance.
Retain full precision internally; display cents. If actual cents-rounded lender schedules are offered, give them a separate explicit rule.

currentDefinitionEvidence.description: Estimate rental cash flow, capitalization rate, and cash-on-cash return.

modes.title: Rental property analysis
modes.formula: NOI = effective rental income−operating expenses. Cash flow deducts debt service; cap rate = annual NOI/price.
modes.explanation: Operating expenses should include maintenance, insurance, taxes, and management, but exclude mortgage payments and depreciation.

inputContract.downPercent: Financing equity percentage,100 for all cash
inputContract.afterRepairValue: Optional market value for appreciation projection
inputContract.vacancyPercent: Applied to rental income only in this model
inputContract.managementPercent: Share of effective collected rental+other income
inputContract.expenseLines: Annual amounts and independent annual growth rates for tax,insurance,HOA,maintenance,other

conventions: Initial investor cash = down payment + closing + repairs. Repairs affect cash invested, not automatically market value.
NOI excludes debt service; investor cashflow subtracts actual mortgage payments. Cap rate and cash-on-cash return have different denominators.
Appreciation starts from afterRepairValue if specified, otherwise purchasePrice. Do not add repair cash again to afterRepairValue.
Yearly operations are modeled as year-end investor cashflows; monthly amortization supplies debt service and exit balance.
Exit sale proceeds join the final year operating cashflow; do not count recovered down payment or principal a second time.
No income taxes, depreciation deductions, recapture, capital-gains taxes or investment return guarantees are implied.
formulaSteps: Year y: rent=12*monthlyRent*(1+rentGrowth)^(y-1); collectedRent=rent*(1-vacancy).
OtherIncome=12*otherMonthlyIncome*(1+otherIncomeGrowth)^(y-1); management=managementRate*(collectedRent+otherIncome).
NOI=collectedRent+otherIncome-management-sum(expenseLine_y). Cashflow=NOI-actualDebtService_y.
Sale=knownPrice or startingMarketValue*(1+appreciation)^holdingYears. NetExit=Sale*(1-saleCost)-remainingDebt.
IRR solves investor cashflow series[-initialCash,CF1,...CFH+NetExit]. Show all supported roots/no-root as appropriate. TotalProfit=sum(netCashflows); totalROI=profit/initialCash.
validation: Do not continue mortgage payments after actual payoff.
If initialCash=0, cash-on-cash and total ROI are undefined; retain valid dollar outputs.
Negative net sale proceeds represent additional exit cash needed.
Require integer holding years for this annual model, or a separate partial-year convention.
